details.body: JustB Baba, a Peranakan eatery in Marine Parade and second outlet from the family behind Marie's Lapis Cafe, offers heritage Nyonya cooking alongside traditional pork dishes and handmade kuehs. Located a 5-minute walk from Marine Parade MRT station, it is best suited for families, multi-generational gatherings, and casual diners seeking authentic home-style flavours in a neighbourhood setting.

Wah Eng Beef Noodles has opened its first food court stall at Food Opera in ION Orchard, serving dry or soup beef noodles with beef brisket, tendon, tripe and beef balls. Prices start from S$8.90 for handmade beef ball soup and S$15.90 for signature noodles, making it a useful option for those seeking traditional beef noodles in a central location.

Family Hakata, a halal-certified mookata stall at Ang Mo Kio Avenue 6, offers a S$19.90 per pax deal for a minimum of 2 people, covering seafood, marinated meats and lok-lok items with no time limit. Crab and young lobster fit the pan poorly, while the lok-lok and chilli sauces stand out. The deal suits diners seeking variety at a fixed price.

Kiap Kiap is a new fried chicken bar in Bugis
Image credit: Kiap Kiap
My guilty pleasure after a late-night KTV sesh with my friends is almost always fried chicken. In fact, I’m probably Wingstop’s number one fan . My gripe, though, is that they close early, which isn’t ideal for my supper plans . If you’re like me, Kiap Kiap is a new fried chicken bar in Bugis you have to check out.
10 Best Late-Night Supper Spots In The East For Dim Sum, Wok Hei Ramen & More
Image credit: Kiap Kiap
Decked out in retro-inspired red-and-white decor and LED lights, the space aims to create a vibey spot for people to connect over good food and drinks. There are even card games to keep you entertained if you ever get bored.
Image credit: Kiap Kiap
Food-wise, they specialise in all things fried chicken. Their signature Kiap Kiap’s Original Fried Chicken ($12++) features two pieces of golden-brown fried chicken. The chicken is said to be juicy and moist inside, while the exterior breading is shatteringly crunchy and seasoned with a secret blend of spices.
Image credit: Kiap Kiap
If you’re looking to spice things up, there are also other fried chicken flavours to try. Mala addicts should definitely go for their Duck Fat Mala Fried Chicken ($14++) , comprising the same two pieces of fried chicken drenched in a spicy, savoury mala chilli oil made by simmering Sichuan peppercorns and other spices in duck fat.
Image credit: ANGELINE CHU SU LING via Google Maps
Those who can’t get enough of Genki Sushi’s mentaiko mayo should order the Mentaiko Fried Chicken With Ikura ($18++) , drizzled generously with creamy mentaiko mayo, then torched and garnished with ikura for a satisfying pop of flavour.
Image credit: Kiap Kiap
Fried chicken isn’t all that they serve, though, and it’ll be remiss of me to not share about their sides. Online reviews claim that their King’s Truffle Poutine ($20++) is a must-try: crispy yet fluffy fries topped with dollops of truffle mayo, a sunny-side-up fried egg, black truffle, and parmesan, all doused in umami beef gravy.
Image credit: Kiap Kiap
Get their Hot Mozzarella ($12++) for some seriously satisfying cheese pulls; here, you get stretchy mozzarella coated in a light breading and served with a tangy raspberry sauce for a sweet-and-savoury combo.
Image credit: Kiap Kiap
Otherwise, try their Seafood Jenny’s Udon ($16++) , a dish inspired by the founder’s mum. Meant to be shared round the table, it comes packed with springy udon noodles stir-fried with eggs and a medley of seafood, including scallops, squid, prawns, and octopus. It’s said to have a strong wok hei taste that’s reminiscent of hokkien mee .
Image credit: Kiap Kiap
Round things off with the Banana Pudding ($6++) , served tableside: a heaping scoop of caramelised bananas and mascarpone sandwiched between layers of ladyfingers, topped with Biscoff cookie crumbs.
Image credit: @kiapkiap.sg
If cocktails are your thing, they’ve got a solid lineup of speciality drinks. Their signature, the Babygirl ($22++) , was originally curated by one of the founders for his wife, blending Patron Silver tequila with elderflower and raspberry.
Image credit: Kiap Kiap
Kiap Kiap also hosts monthly events. In October, they will be hosting Girl’s Night every Wednesday from 6pm to 11:30pm, which comes with free-flow truffle fries, 1-for-1 promotion for all gin and tonic beverages, and a complimentary tarot card reading with a minimum spend of $50 per person , just in time for the spooky season of Halloween!
The restaurant is a four-minute walk away from Bugis MRT Station .
My hot take: Based on personal experience, the earthy notes of matcha balance out the richness of fried chicken, so after your meal, get your matcha fix at Little Rituals , located a nine-minute walk away. If you’re not so adventurous, you can check out our guide to the best food in Bugis instead for more eats in the locale.

A shopping spree at MUJI can leave you feeling peckish, but also not wanting to spend any more than you just did. Good thing that you can get 15% off their cafe’s regular-priced a la carte dishes with a minimum of $10 spent. Their menu is on the healthier side, so you won’t have to worry about indulging in 2 pieces of their Hokkaido potato croquette. Otherwise, you can also choose from their cold deli menu’s assortment of salads. To sweeten your day further, you can also get 10% off their regular-priced clothes & household items with the same amount of minimum spend. Just remember to key in your birthdate in the Muji passport before your birth month, and you will get the discount coupon on the 10th of your birthday month.

Osteria Da Su opens at 163 Telok Ayer Street on Friday 23 October 2026, with 25 sharing plates from S$14++ that fold Korean accents into classic Italian cooking. The casual osteria is the newest restaurant from NAE:UM Group , next door to its one-Michelin-starred Korean fine-dining sibling NAE:UM, and is run by Korea-born Chef Suji Park.
Photo: Osteria Da Su
Opening week is dinner only. From 16 November the kitchen plans Monday to Saturday lunch and dinner. Bookings go through the restaurant’s reservation link at bit.ly/dasu.
Who is cooking
Park has cooked Italian food for close to 20 years, including stints in Bergamo, Milan and Sicily, three years at three-Michelin-starred Da Vittorio in Bergamo, two years at Claudio Sadler’s Milan trattoria, and time on the opening team of Massimo Bottura’s Gucci Osteria in Seoul. She and NAE:UM chef founder Louis Han met as students at Korea Tourism College and have been friends for 16 years. The Telok Ayer unit next to NAE:UM came up for lease in June 2026, and they opened the Italian room together.
The name works in two languages. In Italian, “da Su” reads as an osteria from Su. In Korean, “da su” means many people, which is how the kitchen frames a neighbourhood table rather than a tasting counter.
What is on the menu
Handmade pasta sits at the centre of the list. Spaghetti alle vongole is S$28++, built on asari clam stock with Korean water parsley (minari) in place of Italian parsley, and the shells removed before service. Tortelli di galbi jjim is S$30++, with Korean braised pork inside handmade tortelli and sage butter. Farfalle all’amatriciana is S$24++, finished with guanciale chips brushed in gochujang bulgogi sauce.
Photo: Osteria Da Su
Smaller plates start lower. Korean pepper fritto, a fried gochu chilli stuffed with prawn and ricotta and served with doenjang mayonnaise and balsamic soy, is S$14++. Zucchini bruschetta is S$12++, and insalata condiglione with a Korean soy-marinated egg is S$18++. For dessert, dalgona tiramisu is S$14++, a classic mascarpone and savoiardi tiramisu topped with housemade dalgona honeycomb, and salame di cioccolato is S$10++.
Photo: Osteria Da Su
The room
The restaurant seats 34: eight at the kitchen counter, 16 on banquettes and ten in a raised lounge. The fit-out mixes arched openings, terracotta floors and warm wood with a cleaner Korean line, and framed photographs Park took in Italy hang on the walls. Diners walk past the open kitchen on the way in.
Telok Ayer Street is a short walk from Telok Ayer and Downtown MRT stations. The group’s other sibling restaurant is GU:UM, a modern Korean steakhouse, which makes the Italian room its first non-Korean concept in Singapore. Prices carry a 10 per cent service charge and GST. The restaurant is not halal-certified.

Rawr Cafe is a new tiger-themed cafe in Jalan Besar
Wunderfolks , the mastermind behind Oh Wunder Cafe and Cafe Barco , is back with another concept. Its latest venture, Rawr Cafe , opened in Jalan Besar on 17 October 2027 . Unlike the other two concepts, this new cafe offers locally inspired brunch fare in a cute tiger-themed setup.
The cafe interior features adorable red-and-white tiger graphics.
You’ll also find a display of merchandise, from their house-made kaya to a tiger-inspired cap and stickers.
The menu features local flavours in the form of Western brunch classics. Some must-tries recommended by the cafe are the Singaporean Breakfast Latte ($8++) , Nasi Lemak Chicken Burger ($18++), Laksa Cream Halibut ($24++), Gula Melaka Pandan Cloud ($8++), Tiger Bomb ($12++), and Soft Shell Crab Chilli Pasta ($23++).
The Soft Shell Crab Chilli Pasta was served with a whole crab. The tomato-based sauce was sweet, tangy, and mildly spicy. Personally, it tasted more like regular red pasta sauce than chilli crab.
The soft-shell crab appeared to be lightly battered and deep-fried, giving it a crispy exterior. Beneath the shell was tender, fleshy crab meat with some creamy roe. The crab had some natural sweetness and brininess that came through nicely.
The Nasi Lemak Chicken Burger was extremely hearty, layered with fried chicken, fresh lettuce, and cucumber, then topped with ikan bilis and sambal for that bold umami flavour.
For sides, we got the Prawn Paste Chicken ($15++) . It tasted like regular har cheong gai—the exterior was fried till crisp, coating the greasy, tender chicken wing. I noticed that the chicken meat was a little pinker than what I was used to, so I thought it could’ve been cooked for longer.
We also got two of the signature drinks: the SG Breakfast Latte, a creamy pandan latte, and Tiger Bomb, espresso topped with orange foam.
Image credit: Rawr Cafe
You can also choose to top your drinks with an adorable Raw Tiger Cookie Topper for just $2++!
The SG Breakfast Latte caught our eye with its e foamy “fried egg” on top. It’s served with a crunchy slab of kaya toast, which was light, fragrant, and perfect for soaking up the latte. FYI: the “yolk” in the foam is kaya-flavoured!
The Tiger Bomb had an intense citrusy flavour, thanks to the addition of the orange-infused foam. Paired with espresso, it made for a unique flavour combination that’s worth trying.
Overall, Rawr Cafe is definitely worth a visit if you love cutesy cafes. The SG Breakfast Latte is my favourite in terms of taste and appearance, so give it a go!

Have you passed by Spicy Hubby at Centrepoint Food Street and realised that the stall’s name rings a bell? That’s because it belongs to the same founder who owns Spicy Wife , a popular Malaysian-style nasi lemak stall at Amoy Street Food Centre that attracts long snaking queues during lunchtime.
Boasting a retro charm, the 60-seater eatery evokes the nostalgic vibe of Heap Seng Leong Coffeeshop with its signature blue-and-white tiled walls. Besides its faux retro-style windows, the space even displays old-fashioned toys and snacks for sale, just like those mama stalls that I frequented when I was still in primary school. Everything is self-service here, from placing your order at the kiosk to collecting your food.
What to order at Spicy Hubby
We started off with one of their new additions — the Nasi Ayam Gepuk (S$12.90) . A bed of nasi lemak was crowned with a whole battered chicken thigh that’s drizzled with kicap manis , served with a sunny-side-up, peanut gravy and sambal .
Just look at how glorious that chicken thigh was! Ginormous and coated in a golden-brown batter that didn’t look overly greasy, the chicken definitely made a great first impression. Unfortunately, the meat itself was devoid of any seasoning. It was only when enjoyed with the skin that the faint, sweet notes of the kicap manis truly came through.
However, pairing the chicken with the peanut sauce and s ambal combo was a game-changer in the best way possible. The peanut sauce that reminded me of the thick renditions served at hotpot places was rich and nutty, while the shiok , fiery sambal came in hot and ready to rumble. Try them together for yourself — you’ll get exactly what I mean! The rice was equally well executed, with fluffy grains and a robust coconut fragrance that tied everything nicely.
Next on our agenda was the other new kid on the block — the Nasi Rendang Ayam (S$12.90) . Sitting alongside the nasi lemak was a generous portion of chicken rendang pieces sprinkled with desicated coconut, accompanied by prawn keropok and a fried egg.
The rendang doesn’t taste like the usual ones that I have at nasi padang spots. It was saucy and undeniably unique, in a good way, with an interesting enough flavour that kept me going back for more. Those who don’t particularly enjoy fried food in general might prefer this more.
Of course, we had to get the signature Nasi Goreng Ayam Berempah (S$9.90) , a dish that made them popular at their flagship CBD hawker stall. This nasi lemak combo with a whole slab of spiced fried chicken was slightly more traditional than the other two. It came with the usual ikan bilis -peanut combo, fried egg, and sambal .
My dining partners had visited Spicy Wife before, but this was my first time trying it. Compared to the earlier Nasi Ayam Gepuk , this rendition boasted a far superior marinade. The flesh was well-seasoned, while the crispy skin was infused with an aromatic array of spices that added a ton of flavour without overwhelming the palate. The few pieces of fried curry leaves also gave an extra boost of fragrance to the chicken.
The sambal might’ve looked intimidating by its colour, but it’s actually mild with a slight hint of sweetness.
We also tried a number of their sides. The XL Otak (S$4.90) , Long Bean Sambal (S$4.90) , and Curry Fish Ball (S$6.90) .
My favourite was the Curry Fish Ball , which had a flavoursome curry and QQ fishballs. It may not look like much, but give me anything with curry and I’ll polish everything off. It tasted like the ones I had on my last Hong Kong trip. As for the XL Otak , it fell a little flat in the flavour department. If only the fish paste and spices were a tad stronger; it would’ve been much better.
Looking for a sweet little deal? Here’s one for you — from 16 to 18 Oct 2026 , Spicy Hubby is having a 1-for-1 Promotion on their 3 mains that I had just mentioned.
Who Spicy Hubby is best for
It’s perfect for non-traditionalists who have a craving for Malaysian-style nasi lemak and want to pair it with unique protein options.
How to get there?
You can take the MRT, alight at Somerset MRT Station (NS23) and head towards Centrepoint Food Street. It can get a little confusing, so go to the basement of Centrepoint, and look out for the escalator that will lead u to the Food Street. Alternatively, there are bus services bringing you to the nearest bus stops: Orchard Plaza and Opp Somerset Stn .
Do we recommend Spicy Hubby?
If you’re in the area, then Spicy Hubby is definitely worth checking out. However, with a few hits and misses, I wouldn’t specially travel all the way there just to savour a plate of Malaysian-style nasi lemak .

From $3.20++ Genki Sushi's Crayon Shinchan collaboration runs from 24 September to 8 November 2026, with 14 limited-time dishes led by a Signature Cheesy Ebi Fry Taco at $3.20, a Shinchan Cheeky Chicken Katsu Rice at $8.90, a Miso Butter Corn Ramen at $8.60 and an Azuki Matcha Jelly Soft Serve at $6.90. Every $50 spent earns a gachapon-style spin for Genki vouchers, a Shinchan cup holder, phone strap or cable clips, so the collectibles are luck of the draw rather than something you can buy. The two things you can buy are a Shinchan Thermal Lunch Bag ($10.90, or $7.90 with a DBS/POSB card and $6.90 for Genki members) and a Shinchan hoodie at $25.90 that only members can get. Menu prices are before 10% service charge and GST, so the $3.20 taco is about $3.84 nett, and Genki's free app membership pays for itself on the lunch bag alone.

$6 whisky Sushi Tei's Jewel Changi Airport outlet (#03-209) has reopened after a refit, and it is marking the new look with two back-to-back dine-in specials. From Monday 19 to Sunday 25 October 2026, a glass of Kirin Fuji Sanroku 50 Degree whisky is $6, limited to the first 20 orders a day. From Monday 26 October to Sunday 1 November, a subtotal of at least $60 gets three free pieces of salmon sashimi, capped at 100 redemptions a day. Both are Jewel-only, dine-in only and while stocks last.

If you frequent Starbucks often, you would know about this freebie. For the uninitiated, you can sign up for free as a Starbucks Rewards member and claim a free slice of cake with a purchase of any drink. If you’re a Gold Tier member, you’ll also be able to enjoy a free drink on top of the cake.

Broth and Bowls Ramen is a one-man, hole-in-the-wall Japanese eatery located within Oxley Tower in Singapore's Central Business District. The weekday-only spot serves affordable tonkotsu pork-bone ramen, black garlic noodles with blowtorched chashu, unagi udon, and curry rice bowls priced between S$11.90 and S$14.90. It is best suited for CBD office workers seeking a quiet, budget-friendly lunch, though early visits are recommended as popular dishes often sell out before the end of peak hours.

Ducoo is a newly opened hawker stall at North Bridge Road Market & Food Centre in Lavender, run by young chefs Javier and Ronald. The stall serves restaurant-quality Italian pasta, featuring dishes like Prawn Aglio with daily market-bought tiger prawns and Tagliatelle Bolognese Ragu. It is ideal for diners seeking authentic, wallet-friendly Italian meals within a traditional hawker setting.

Redeem a free lobster when you purchase an Olympian bucket set (U.P. $254) at Cajun on Wheels , which can easily feed a group of 6. No membership is required, but ensure you book the table in advance and indicate “birthday lobster” so they can prepare it for you. Don’t try to cheat cause they will ask for a valid photo ID of the birthday girl/boy.

GENTLEWOMAN is a Thai fashion label best known for its iconic canvas bags featuring bold typography of its brand name. Shop them in person at their Singapore store! While you’re there, explore their other bag collections alongside their signature canvas styles.
My personal favourite is the Jelly Rush collection with jelly bags that evoke a nostalgic Y2K (2000s) feeling. Plus, these jelly bags come in trendy prints and colours like polka dot and mint green.

If you have more bags than you can ever hold in your lifetime, browse their range of clothing collections instead. A star collection you can find here is Dormitory Darlings , a collaboration with Thai actress and model Chompoo Araya . This collection features bows and coquette-style clothing, perfect for the demure girls, or should I say, gentle women.
Other collections include Echoes Of Refinement, which explores modern elegance through clean, sharp tailoring, and Theory Of The Wind, featuring fluid silhouettes and lightweight fabrics great for Singapore’s weather.

Free gift Food Junction turns 33 with a Picnic Party: spend $33 at any of its food courts (up to 3 same-day receipts combined) and the outlet manager hands you a free limited-edition Food Junction x Coca-Cola 33rd Anniversary Food Jar, from 1 to 31 October 2026 while stocks last. Buy a Coca-Cola drink after that and you also get a free can-opener keychain. Its $5 Weekday Saver Meals, one dish per outlet per weekday, now run to 31 December.

Briyani is one of the most satisfying dishes around, so why not have as much as you like? Indian Saaga on Race Course Road is offering unlimited briyani for S$38++ for two, which works out to S$19++ per person. Now that’s a steal! This deal is only available from 12pm – 6pm (Mon to Sat).
Credit – Google
Located at 38 Race Course Road, Indian Saaga is a halal-certified North Indian restaurant serving tried-and-true classics. It prides itself on affordable prices, so this deal comes as no surprise.
Some of you might recognise Indian Saaga, as it shares founders with The Song of India. That restaurant became Singapore’s first Indian restaurant to receive a Michelin star in 2016. Indian Saaga focuses on a family vibe, with big tables and plenty of seats for larger groups.
This deal, however, breaks that convention, as it is intended for pairs. So if you have a special someone, or just a buddy you want to hang out with, this deal is perfect for you.
Credit – Indian Saaga via Instagram
The deal includes 90 minutes of unlimited briyani , with a choice of chicken or mutton. Diners also get unlimited mutton curry, papad and raita , plus a 1-time serving of plain, butter or garlic naan .
Credit – Indian Saaga via Instagram
Briyani aside, the menu also has kebabs , curries and fresh naans .
Some of their popular dishes are the Mutton dum biryani (S$18++) , Chicken tikka masala (S$16++) and Goan fish curry (S$16++) . So, if you happen to feel peckish for something else, peruse the menu and maybe try something new.
Indian Saaga is open daily from 12pm – 11pm, and reservations can be made online at indiansaaga.com or via WhatsApp
at +65 9789 9004.
This deal is available for a limited time only, from 12pm – 6pm (Mon to Sat) . Head down to Indian Saaga for a hearty briyani meal.

34% OFF PrimaDeli, the halal bakery chain owned by Neo Group, turns 34 this October and has cut three of its best-selling fresh cream cakes by 34%. The Large Blackforest Classic, Truffle and Fruit Paradise cakes (1kg, 10-15 people) are $33.50 instead of $50.80 until 31 October 2026, in its outlets and online. That is $1.30 less than the same cakes in Regular size, which serves 6-8. The Premium Pandan Chiffon Cake, now on an upgraded recipe, is 15% off at $19.50 (usual $23), and seven more pandan treats are 15% off online. Online orders need four working days, a $50 minimum and an $18 delivery fee.

$9.90 + 30% off Matchaya's 10.10 sale cuts its Matcha 18 powder to $9.90 for a 30g tin (usually $19) and takes 30% off everything else, from ceremonial matcha and tea boxes to chasen whisks and soft serve tubs. Its Instagram post says the deal runs to Sunday 11 October at 11.59pm at its Tiong Bahru and Suntec outlets and on matchaya.sg, while the online store's own banner runs it to Tuesday 13 October. Online, the discount applies at checkout and delivery is free only above $100 after discount.

23g protein from $6.90 PlayMade has launched its first Protein Smoothie Series, a limited-time line at all 28 Singapore stores from 9 October 2026, still available while stocks last. Food prices are the highest they’ve ever been. Even a simple lunch in Singapore suffers from wildly high prices. Which is why I was surprised to see Mexican-inspired dishes , famous for their expensive price tag, only cost S$4.90 a piece at The Daily Fiesta in Bedok . And it’s Halal-certified as well.
But are they actually good? I went down to their second outlet to have a taste myself. I’d like to think I make pretty awesome tacos and quesadillas , so I think I’m qualified for the task ahead.
What to order at The Daily Fiesta
With the prices being so affordable, I decided to try a few of their staples. I ordered the Cajun Chicken Taco (S$4.90) , Crispy Fish Taco (S$4.90) , Chicken Quesadilla (S$13) and Beef Quesadilla (S$14) . All of them include a side of salsa and guacamole.
Let’s start with the Cajun chicken taco (S$4.90) . This one was quite a letdown compared to the other dishes. Firstly, the slaw. I found it too sweet, and it overpowered a lot of the other ingredients, namely the chicken. On top of that, they also added corn, which only made it sweeter. I would suggest replacing the slaw with regular iceberg lettuce for a more balanced flavour.
I also felt the quail egg on top was a little unnecessary, but that’s just me.
The Crispy Fish Taco (S$4.90) was much better. It had a beautifully crispy battered fish laid on top of their slaw. On top of that was a creamy sauce with a bit of spice, black ebiko and fried shallots. The flavours were a medley of sweet, salty and tart, all working in harmony. The black ebiko also added a nice popping texture when I bit into it. All in all, one of the better fish tacos I’ve had in recent memory.
Lavi Tacos: Hidden Mexican gem at Chinatown with rare birria tacos & delicious taco platters
Now, let’s move on to the quesadillas.
The Chicken Quesadilla (S$13) was pretty solid. They seared a cheese crust within the tortilla, giving an intense grilled cheese flavour. The Cajun chicken flavour was more prominent here, but I felt it still lacked intensity. As a whole, though, it was still very yummy, especially when dipped in their salsa . I would recommend increasing the spices for the Cajun chicken or marinating it for longer. Also, while the salsa was tangy with a refreshing tomato flavour, the guacamole was a bit on the sour side. It could use a bit of salt to bring out the avocado flavour.
Now this is a quesadilla! The Beef Quesadilla (S$14) was everything I wanted it to be and more. It still had the same formula: a cheese crust inside the tortilla, stringy and soft cheese, and a protein. However, the meat? Ay dios mio , it was perfectly seasoned. It had smoky, slightly spicy and rich flavours when melted together with the cheese. The meat had a bite to it, not too soft, which was my original worry.
It had to have a high fat content as well, as there was so much grease at the bottom. This is a telltale sign of a good quesadilla. Even the tortilla seems darker than the chicken version. I suspect the grease really absorbed into the tortilla, making the beef flavour very prominent in every bite.
Who is The Daily Fiesta best for?
Honestly, anyone who likes a decent Mexican lunch. I struggle to find someone who doesn’t fit in this category. Even vegetarians have options, as they have a mushroom quesadilla and taco. On top of that, they also have a variety of pastas, sides like corn ribs and much more. If you’re looking for a delicious lunch, you can’t go wrong with The Daily Fiesta.
How to get to The Daily Fiesta
Luckily for all of us, their Bedok outlet is near Bedok Mall. There is also a bus stop a few metres away called After Heartbeat @ Bedok , with several buses leading there. Alternatively, you can take the MRT to Bedok. The Daily Fiesta is only an 8-minute walk from the MRT station.
Do we recommend The Daily Fiesta?
Good food and better prices. It’s going to be hard for me not to recommend this spot. The amount of options alone makes this place worth a visit. But if I had to point to one specific dish, it has to be their Beef Quesadilla (S$14) . It really is a level above the rest, though I’m sure you will find your own favourites when you get there.
Do note that they sell out fast . I arrived an hour after opening, and their Beef Bolo Tacos were already sold out and I just managed to get their beef quesadilla , so clearly the beef is a fan favourite.

The six dishes and what they cost
• Jigoku Ribeye, S$68: seared Oita Wagyu with seasonal local vegetables, smoked Japanese burrata and a spicy hot sauce butter
• Kabosu Coast, S$24: yellowtail ceviche with leche de tigre, papadum chips and Secai Marche Japanese burrata
• Tiger Nashi, S$18: gyoza filled with Himeshima tiger prawns and Hita pears, with a pineapple chipotle sauce
• Shiitake Claypot, S$32: braised sweet Oita shiitake with assorted mushrooms over butter rice
• Himeshima “Hae” Mee, S$18: tiger prawns in Japanese udon, done Singapore-style
• Sweet Potato O’ Mine, S$12: a tart made with Oita sweet potato, topped with cheese mousse
Himeshima “Hae” Mee swaps yellow noodles for udon, at S$18. Photo: Kinki Restaurant + Bar
Where the menu leans
Jigoku means hell, the name Beppu gives its boiling hot spring pools, and the ribeye is the one dish built to match it with a spicy butter. It is also the only one over S$35, so most of the menu sits at small-plate prices.
The two prawn dishes are the most Singaporean ideas on the card. Hae mee is a prawn noodle dish most readers will know from a hawker centre; here it swaps yellow noodles for udon and uses prawns from Himeshima, a small island off Oita’s coast. The gyoza pairs the same prawns with pears from Hita, an inland Oita city.
Burrata appears twice, in the ribeye and the ceviche, both times a Japanese-made cheese.
How it compares with the regular menu
The Oita dishes are priced close to Kinki’s everyday dinner card. The Shiitake Claypot is S$2 more than the restaurant’s Magic Mushroom Claypot at S$30, and the Kabosu Coast ceviche is S$2 less than the Hamachi Crudo, another yellowtail starter, at S$26.
The regular Ohmi Wagyu Hoba-yaki, an A4 striploin with mushrooms, is S$90 for one person, against S$68 for the Oita cut. The prawn gyoza is S$18, against S$32 for the Wagyu Foie Gras Gyoza on the main menu.
The Shiitake Claypot is S$32, S$2 more than Kinki’s regular mushroom claypot. Photo: Kinki Restaurant + Bar
The claypot is the one meat-free-looking main, though the menu carries no vegetarian, halal or allergen labels.
Booking and getting there
Kinki takes reservations on its website. The restaurant is in Customs House on Collyer Quay, a short walk from Raffles Place MRT, with the Kinki rooftop bar upstairs. The Oita dishes are served at the restaurant from Thursday 15 October until Saturday 31 October.

Potatoes are a beloved staple for many, myself included. With their versatility, you can cook them in so many ways — boiled, mashed, fried — you name it, it probably yields delicious results. If your favourite potato dish is rosti , you’ll be happy to hear that Hippopotato has opened its first physical store in Punggol .
Previously a popular home-based business selling a large variety of rosti with 5.0 stars across 516 Google reviews (at the time of writing), the owners have decided to open up shop in Northshore Plaza I . Their original home-based outlet in Tampines will be closed until further notice, with plans to resume business there once the Punggol store can run independently.
The rosti store is helmed by 2 brothers, Gary Wong and James Wong. Born into a family of cooks and hawkers, the brothers said in an Instagram post , “Food has always been a big part of our DNA”. Hence, they started Hippopotato in 2025 with the goal of making yummy rosti accessible to all.
Fun fact: They used to run a cai fan stall at a Junior College. Plus, James used to be a Marche chef at, you guessed it… the rosti station. Without further ado, here’s what I tried at Hippopotato.
I started with their Golden Classic Rosti (S$5) and opted for sour cream. The usual price for this is S$8 , but to celebrate their grand opening, the first 50 customers can get it for S$5 . This promotion runs from 15 to 18 Oct 2026 , while stocks last.
The rostis were made to order, thus having a perfectly crisp exterior with a nice char that added smokiness to every bite. The potatoes were soft and delicate on the interior, creating a nice medley of textures. When topped with the sour cream, it adds a piquancy to the mild dish. Personally, I prefer it with a heaping spoonful of the sour cream.
The next rosti I tried was the O konomirosti (S$10.50) . This dish is the lovechild of popular Japanese dish o konomiyaki and rosti , inheriting the positives of both parents. As you can see in the picture above, Hippopotato is extremely generous with the bonito flakes given.
Beneath the flakes are also generous drizzles of tangy okonomiyaki sauce and Japanese mayonnaise. This was my favourite as each bite just brought such intense goodness to my taste buds. Bold and savoury from the bonito flakes and okonomiyaki sauce, slightly creamy from the mayonnaise — just wow.
Aside from rosti , Hippopotato also has a range of potato-based sides, such as tater tots and fries. I opted for the Mentaiko Mayo Tater Tots (S$5) . I’m a huge mentaiko fan, but I find typical mentaiko sauces lack the same umami as the actual pollack roe.
Luckily for me, the sauce hits the spot. Slightly spicy with a rich, briny flavour, it complemented the crispy tater tots well. The only thing I wished for was more sauce; there’s an option for the sauce to be on the side for an additional S$0.30, which I will probably go for in the future.
Would I recommend Hippopotato ? Definitely. With amazing rosti and sides, why not #supportlocal while enjoying good food?

The masks can be obtained via mask vending machines or at Community Clubs (CCs) island-wide. The machines are available at selected public transport hubs , Social Service Offices and People’s Association (PA) venues .
The initiative supports vulnerable Singaporeans during severe haze. N95 masks filter fine particles, including PM2.5, a primary pollutant during haze episodes.
Who is eligible for free N95 masks?

• Pioneer Generation (PG)
• Merdeka Generation (MG)
• CHAS Orange/Blue card holders
• Medical Fee Exemption Card (MFEC) holders
• ComCare Assistance recipients
• Pregnant women
• Children aged 7 – 16 years old
• Individuals with medical conditions such as asthma

Sushiro has put three premium plates on a limited menu across its Singapore restaurants from 7 October to 3 November 2026.
Sushiro’s limited premium-plate menu runs to 3 November 2026. Photo: Sushiro Singapore
Sushiro Singapore prices the Aburi Wild Blackthroat Seaperch at S$3.90++, Sous Vide Tender Roast Beef at S$5.90++, and Bancha Braised Octopus at S$3.90++, while stocks last. Prices differ at the Mandai Wildlife Reserve Digiro outlet.
What is on the plate
The seaperch is lightly salted and gently seared for a fatty, umami finish. The roast beef is seasoned with salt and slow-cooked sous vide to keep it tender. The octopus uses Hokkaido mizudako boiled in bancha, roasted green tea, so the tea aroma sits beside the seafood rather than covering it.
The limited plates sit on top of Sushiro’s usual conveyor-belt list of more than 100 sushi and side dishes. Diners still order by touchscreen or from the belt as usual; the three items are the dated add-ons for this window.
Outlets and timing
Orchard Gateway’s Sushiro is at 227 Orchard Road, #B1-07/08. Hougang Mall at 90 Hougang Avenue 10, #02-23/24, opens on 1 October 2026. Most mall outlets run 11am to 10pm with last order at 9.30pm; Jewel Changi opens from 10am.
The premium-plate run continues islandwide at participating restaurants through 3 November, or until stocks run out. The regular menu runs from tuna and grilled salmon to ramen and desserts, with seasonal Japanese specials rotating through the year.
Booking a table
Reservations are taken only through the Sushiro mobile app, where diners pick an arrival time and get a queue number in advance. Takeaway is available at the outlets. The chain opened Japan’s first conveyor-belt sushi restaurant in 1984 and now serves more than 100 varieties of fresh sushi, ramen, desserts and seasonal specials in Singapore.

If you prefer your snacks in smaller portions, Mini Munchi comes in boxes of 6 , perfect for sharing or sampling a few flavours. Traditional Min Jiang Kueh is also available for those who prefer to keep things classic.
They offer vegan options, too. With old-school favourites sitting alongside more unconventional combinations, Munchi Pancakes’ JB debut gives apam balik fans in Malaysia plenty to explore. The big question is, what flavours are you looking forward to the most?

Chef Johanne Siy’s debut restaurant, Árō, prices its Chef’s Tasting Menu at S$268++ a head at 15 Mohamed Sultan Road, while over at The Singapore EDITION on Cuscaden Road, Tanica charges S$48++ for a three-course weekday lunch. Árō ‘s cooking is Creator’s Cuisine, built on lesser-known ingredients from across Asia-Pacific. Tanica cooks Southeast Asian food over a Josper grill and in the wok, meant for sharing.
Photo: Árō
The two sit at opposite ends of a night out near Orchard and River Valley, one a counter-led tasting room and the other a hotel dining room open from breakfast. Further out on Dempsey Hill, Petra opens its Mediterranean dining room on 24 October .
Árō on Mohamed Sultan Road
The name joins two words: arō, Latin for “to plough”, and áro, “love” in the dialect of the chef’s hometown. The room is small, with a counter for 10, two tables of four and a private dining room holding four tables of two. Keiji Ashizawa Design worked it in walnut, rattan, stone and bronze, and the art on the walls comes from Siy’s own collection.
Photo: Árō
For now there is one menu, the Chef’s Tasting Menu at S$268++. A shorter tasting menu is marked as coming soon, without a price yet.
Árō opens Thursday to Monday, with lunch from 12pm to 3pm and dinner from 6pm to 10pm, and closes on Tuesdays and Wednesdays. Bookings go through SevenRooms, and the restaurant also takes enquiries at info@arosingapore.com.
Tanica at The Singapore EDITION
Tanica is the EDITION’s all-day restaurant at 38 Cuscaden Road, organised around herbs, spices and fire. Breakfast runs from 6.30am to 10.30am and lunch from 12pm to 2.30pm. Dinner is 6pm to 10pm from Monday to Thursday, and to 10.30pm from Friday to Sunday.
Photo: Tanica
The weekday set lunch, Monday to Friday, is three courses for S$48++ with coffee or tea, served within 60 minutes. Booking through SevenRooms comes with three hours of complimentary parking. A wagyu hanger steak main adds S$10, a glass of wine S$15 and a Saicho osmanthus sparkling tea S$12.
On Sundays the restaurant runs Sunday Table at S$98 a person, S$168 with wines, or S$198 with Louis Roederer Collection 246 champagne.
What the Tanica menu costs
The à la carte menu leans on hawker classics reworked for the grill and wok. Hokkaido sea urchin pie tee is S$30. Char kway teow, Singapore laksa noodles and Hainanese chicken rice are S$28 each. The char kway teow contains pork, and other dishes on the menu do too.
Photo: Tanica
The larger plates climb quickly. An asam pedas seafood risotto and Iga Bakar Kicap, a 72-hour wagyu short rib, are S$58 each. A one-kilogram grilled grouper is S$138, the XO mapo tofu with lobster S$128, and a 500g rib eye S$178.
Prices at both restaurants carry a 10 per cent service charge and GST.
Tanica takes reservations on +65 6329 5000 as well as SevenRooms.
